# Verdict: REJECT ## Overall Assessment This component implements the *visual* interaction model of a combobox correctly — typing filters, arrow keys navigate, Enter selects, Escape closes. However, the ARIA pattern is incomplete in ways that make it **unusable by screen reader users**. The listbox container has no `role="listbox"`, options have no `role="option"`, there is no `aria-activedescendant` to track the highlighted item, and no `aria-controls` to link the input to the popup. A screen reader user who opens this list hears a generic "list" (or nothing) with no way to navigate, select, or understand which item is active. This is not a partial gap — it is a complete access failure for one user category. ## Pre-commitment Predictions Before reading the code, I predicted the following for a combobox component: | # | Prediction | Found? | |---|-----------|--------| | 1 | Missing `role="listbox"` on popup container | ✅ Confirmed | | 2 | Missing `role="option"` on individual items | ✅ Confirmed | | 3 | Missing `aria-activedescendant` for active tracking | ✅ Confirmed | | 4 | Missing `aria-controls` linking input → listbox | ✅ Confirmed | | 5 | Missing `aria-selected` on options | ✅ Confirmed | | 6 | ArrowUp handler fires when list is closed (bug) | ✅ Confirmed | | 7 | No Home/End key support | ✅ Confirmed | All seven predictions confirmed. No surprises — the component is a textbook "80% ARIA" implementation. --- ## Critical Findings (Blocks Access) ### C1: Listbox container missing `role="listbox"` **Evidence:** `BuggyCombobox.jsx` — the `
` element (the popup container) has no `role` attribute. **User group impacted:** Screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) **WCAG/APG citation:** WAI-ARIA APG Combobox (list with autocomplete) pattern — the popup MUST have `role="listbox"`. WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value): the role must be programmatically determinable. **Why this matters:** Without `role="listbox"`, screen readers announce this container as a generic group or region. The user cannot enter list navigation mode, cannot use list-specific commands (e.g., JAWS "O" for options, NVDA list navigation), and has no semantic understanding that this is a selectable list. The entire interaction model is invisible to assistive technology. **Fix:** ```jsx
``` **Confidence:** HIGH --- ### C2: Options missing `role="option"` and `aria-selected` **Evidence:** `BuggyCombobox.jsx` — each `
` in the `.map()` has no `role` and no `aria-selected`. **User group impacted:** Screen reader **WCAG/APG citation:** WAI-ARIA APG Combobox pattern — each option MUST have `role="option"`. The active option MUST have `aria-selected="true"`. WCAG 4.1.2. **Why this matters:** Screen readers announce items as "text" or "group" rather than "option." The user cannot distinguish options from other content, cannot use option-specific navigation, and has no way to know which item is currently highlighted. The `selectedIndex` state exists in JavaScript but is never exposed to assistive technology. **Fix:** ```jsx {filtered.map((option, idx) => (
handleSelect(option)} className={selectedIndex === idx ? 'suggestion-item selected' : 'suggestion-item'} > {option}
))} ``` **Confidence:** HIGH --- ### C3: Missing `aria-activedescendant` on the input **Evidence:** `BuggyCombobox.jsx` — the `` element has no `aria-activedescendant` attribute. The `selectedIndex` state is tracked in JS but never communicated to the accessibility tree. **User group impacted:** Screen reader **WCAG/APG citation:** WAI-ARIA APG Combobox pattern — the input MUST use `aria-activedescendant` to reference the ID of the currently highlighted option. This is the mechanism by which screen readers track which option is "active" without moving focus. WCAG 4.1.2. **Why this matters:** In the combobox pattern, focus stays on the input while the user navigates options with arrow keys. The ONLY way a screen reader knows which option is highlighted is through `aria-activedescendant`. Without it, the user presses ArrowDown repeatedly and hears nothing change. They cannot select a specific item by position. This is a complete functional failure for screen reader users. **Fix:** ```jsx = 0 ? `option-${selectedIndex}` : undefined} /> ``` **Confidence:** HIGH --- ### C4: Missing `aria-controls` linking input to listbox **Evidence:** `BuggyCombobox.jsx` — the `` has no `aria-controls` attribute. The listbox has `id="suggestions-popup"` but nothing references it. **User group impacted:** Screen reader **WCAG/APG citation:** WAI-ARIA APG Combobox pattern — the input MUST have `aria-controls` referencing the listbox ID. WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) and 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships). **Why this matters:** Without `aria-controls`, the screen reader has no programmatic link between the combobox input and its popup list. The user cannot discover the relationship, cannot navigate from input to list, and the list appears as an orphaned element in the accessibility tree. **Fix:** Add `aria-controls="suggestions-popup"` to the input (see C3 fix above). **Confidence:** HIGH --- ## Major Findings (Significantly Degrades Experience) ### M1: ArrowUp fires when list is closed — sets invisible state **Evidence:** `BuggyCombobox.jsx`, `handleKeyDown`: ```js } else if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') { e.preventDefault(); const prevIdx = selectedIndex > 0 ? selectedIndex - 1 : filtered.length - 1; setSelectedIndex(prevIdx); } ``` Unlike `ArrowDown` (which checks `if (!isOpen)`), `ArrowUp` does NOT check `isOpen`. If the list is closed and `selectedIndex` is `-1`, pressing ArrowUp sets `selectedIndex` to `filtered.length - 1` — a "selected" index on a list that doesn't exist in the DOM. **User group impacted:** Keyboard-only, screen reader **WCAG/APG citation:** WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) — keyboard interactions must produce expected results. WAI-ARIA APG Combobox: ArrowUp should open the list if closed (mirroring ArrowDown behavior) or be a no-op. **Why this matters:** A keyboard user pressing ArrowUp with the list closed gets no visual feedback (list doesn't open) but internal state is mutated. If they then press Enter, the code checks `selectedIndex >= 0` and calls `handleSelect(filtered[selectedIndex])` — selecting an item the user never saw. This is a silent data-entry error. **Fix:** ```js } else if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') { e.preventDefault(); if (!isOpen) { setIsOpen(true); setSelectedIndex(filtered.length - 1); } else { const prevIdx = selectedIndex > 0 ? selectedIndex - 1 : filtered.length - 1; setSelectedIndex(prevIdx); } } ``` **Confidence:** HIGH --- ### M2: No `aria-live` or announcement when list opens/closes or filters change **Evidence:** `BuggyCombobox.jsx` — no `aria-live` region, no `role="status"`, no announcement mechanism. The only state change communicated is `aria-expanded` toggling. **User group impacted:** Screen reader **WCAG/APG citation:** WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages) — changes of programmatic state must be communicated to assistive technology. WAI-ARIA APG Combobox: the listbox content should be discoverable when it appears. **Why this matters:** When the user types "a" and 3 results appear, a screen reader user hears the `aria-expanded` change (if their SR announces it) but gets no information about what appeared, how many options are available, or what the first option is. They must guess to press ArrowDown. **Fix:** Add a visually-hidden live region that announces result count: ```jsx {isOpen ? `${filtered.length} suggestions available` : ''} ``` Or rely on `aria-activedescendant` + `role="listbox"` to make the content discoverable (preferred per APG). **Confidence:** MEDIUM (mitigated by `aria-activedescendant` if C3 is fixed — the SR can navigate into the list) --- ### M3: Hardcoded IDs create collision risk in multi-instance scenarios **Evidence:** `BuggyCombobox.jsx` — `id="combobox-input"` and `id="suggestions-popup"` are hardcoded strings. The `htmlFor="combobox-input"` references the same hardcoded ID. **User group impacted:** Screen reader (broken associations), all users (broken label association) **WCAG/APG citation:** WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) — labels must be programmatically associated. If two instances exist, `htmlFor` resolves to the first instance's input, breaking the label for the second. **Why this matters:** If this component is rendered twice on a page (e.g., "From" and "To" fields), the second instance's label points to the first instance's input. Screen readers announce the wrong label. The `aria-controls` reference (once added) would also resolve to the wrong listbox. **Fix:** Use `useId()` (React 18+) or a unique ID generator: ```jsx const id = useId(); // ...
``` **Confidence:** HIGH (as a design flaw; impact depends on usage context) --- ### M4: No Home/End key support for list navigation **Evidence:** `BuggyCombobox.jsx`, `handleKeyDown` — only `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp`, `Enter`, `Escape` are handled. No `Home` or `End` keys. **User group impacted:** Keyboard-only, screen reader **WCAG/APG citation:** WAI-ARIA APG Combobox pattern — "Home: Moves focus to the first option in the listbox." "End: Moves focus to the last option in the listbox." **Why this matters:** For a list with 50+ options, a keyboard user must press ArrowDown 50 times to reach the last item. Home/End provide O(1) navigation. This is a standard expectation for list navigation. **Fix:** ```js } else if (e.key === 'Home') { e.preventDefault(); if (isOpen) setSelectedIndex(0); } else if (e.key === 'End') { e.preventDefault(); if (isOpen) setSelectedIndex(filtered.length - 1); } ``` **Confidence:** HIGH --- ## Minor Findings (Friction but Workaround Exists) - **No `aria-label` on the listbox container.** The listbox div has no accessible name.
